title: Secure Communication Channels
objective: Study-guide review — CISSP — Domain 4: Communication and Network Security: Secure Communication Channels.

items: Creates encrypted tunnel over untrusted network (Internet)
Site-to-site — Connects two networks (offices)
Remote access — Connects individual user to network
Full tunnel — All traffic goes through VPN
Split tunnel — Only corporate traffic goes through VPN (risk: unprotected personal traffic)
Network layer (Layer 3) security protocol suite
AH (Authentication Header) — Integrity and authentication only (no encryption)
ESP (Encapsulating Security Payload) — Encryption + integrity + authentication
Transport mode — Encrypts payload only; original IP header visible
Tunnel mode — Encrypts entire original packet; new IP header added

blocks.text: From Stewart: "In tunnel mode, IPSec provides encryption protection for both the payload and message header by encapsulating the entire original LAN protocol packet and adding its own temporary IPSec header." IKE (Internet Key Exchange) establishes the IPsec security association (SA):

items: Phase 1: Establishes secure channel (IKE SA)
Phase 2: Negotiates IPsec SA for data transfer

blocks.title: Exam trap
blocks.text: ⚠️ Exam Trap: AH provides integrity but NO encryption. ESP provides both. AH is incompatible with NAT because it protects the IP header (which NAT modifies). ESP in transport mode works with NAT traversal.

items: TLS (Transport Layer Security) — Current standard (TLS 1.3 is latest)
SSL — Deprecated predecessor (SSL 3.0 was last version)
Operates at Layer 4-5 (between Transport and Application)
Provides encryption, integrity, and server authentication
Uses asymmetric key exchange → symmetric bulk encryption
Client Hello (supported ciphers, random number)
Server Hello (chosen cipher, certificate, random number)
Key exchange (asymmetric encryption)
Session keys derived (symmetric encryption begins)
Removed weak algorithms (RC4, MD5, SHA-1, DES, 3DES)
Reduced handshake to 1-RTT (faster)
Perfect Forward Secrecy (PFS) required
Removed RSA key exchange (only ephemeral Diffie-Hellman)

blocks.title: Exam trap
blocks.text: ⚠️ Exam Trap: SSL is DEPRECATED. All versions of SSL (1.0, 2.0, 3.0) have known vulnerabilities. Only TLS 1.2+ should be used. The exam may still use "SSL/TLS" but know that SSL alone is insecure.

items: L2TP — Layer 2 Tunneling Protocol; no native encryption; usually paired with IPsec
PPTP — Point-to-Point Tunneling Protocol; insecure, deprecated
GRE — Generic Routing Encapsulation; Cisco proprietary; no encryption
SSH — Secure Shell; encrypted tunnel for remote management (port 22)
WireGuard — Modern VPN protocol; fast, simple, strong encryption

blocks.text: From Chapple: "L2TP does not offer native encryption, but it supports the use of payload encryption protocols. Although it isn't required, L2TP is most often deployed using IPSec's ESP for payload encryption." From Stewart: Tunneling "prevents the traffic control devices from blocking or dropping the communication because such devices don't examine the tunneled contents."
